newsitem.title: KENYA: U.N. calls for exemption of Burundi relief aid.
newsitem.headline: U.N. calls for exemption of Burundi relief aid.

text.p: The United Nations has appealed for relief aid to be exempt from sanctions imposed on Burundi by regional states and said the number of people needing help was increasing.

In a statement issued on Friday, Martin Griffiths, U.N. humanitarian coordinator for the Great Lakes region of central Africa, said no fuel had reached aid agencies in Burundi despite a request made to a regional sanctions committee in November.

"We ask that the (national sanctions) committees respect our petition and the very difficult nature of our work in Burundi," he said. "These supplies are indispensable simply to continue delivering aid."

The statement said an emergency shipment of fuel approved in January was expected to arrive in Burundi in mid-March and the Regional Sanctions Coordinating Committee had not addressed all agencies' concerns.

"Besides fuel and spare parts we have applied for exemptions for educational material and hand tools. This represents direct assistance to populations affected by the conflict in Burundi, said Griffiths, adding the committee had failed to respond.
Regional states imposed economic and transport sanctions against land-locked Burundi last July after the Tutsi-dominated army seized power from a civilian Hutu president.

The U.N. statement said agencies were hampered by a shortage of much-needed humanitarian aid while they were faced with increasing numbers of people in need because of conflict reported to have displaced hundreds of thousands in Burundi.
In New York on Wednesday, Griffiths said he had spotted malnutrition among children in Burundi relocated to special areas by that country's Tutsi-led military government.
More than 150,000 people have died in massacres and civil war in Burundi between the army and Hutu rebels since the 1993 assassination of its first freely elected Hutu president.
